raw_response:
I’ve farmed these 7 mu for 47 years. Never went to school, but I know this land like my own kitchen. It’s just me and my husband now — our children work in Shijiazhuang. We’re old, so we have to be careful with our strength and our money. Every yuan we spend on inputs is a yuan we don’t have for medicine or emergencies.

It’s early October, time to plant wheat. I’ll put wheat on all seven mu, same as every year. For seed, I saved most of it from last year’s harvest, but I bought a little fresh from the village shop because some of my saved grain got buggy. I plant about two big scoops per mu — always have, always will.

Before planting, I’ll spread half a big bag of compound fertilizer per mu as my base. That’s the one my neighbor calls “three-in-one” — I don’t know the numbers on the bag, but it’s the pinkish granules. Then in spring, when the wheat starts jointing and if it looks a little yellow, I’ll topdress with about one small bag of urea per two mu. Last year I skipped the topdress to save money and my yield dropped badly. I learned my lesson. Better to spend the money than risk a bad year.

I’ll irrigate the wheat three times: once after planting to settle it in, once at green-up in spring, and once when the grain is filling. The electricity for the pump costs a lot, but wheat needs water. If we get good rain I might skip one, but I usually do three to be safe.

For maize, summer is always a crazy rush. We harvest the wheat in early June and we have less than a week to get the maize in the ground or we miss the season. I’ll buy hybrid seed from the shop — everyone knows you can’t save hybrid seed for next year. I’ll put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant, and if I’m not too tired after the wheat harvest rush, I’ll throw some urea on top later when the maize is knee-high. If I’m too worn out or the hired help isn’t around, I might skip the topdress. The summer rains usually help, so I’ll irrigate once or twice, only if July is dry.

I don’t plan much pesticide. I’ll spray herbicide once on each crop to kill the weeds — I can’t bend down to pull them anymore like I did when I was young. If bugs come, I’ll deal with it then, but I don’t buy insecticide ahead of time.

I expect about 750 jin per mu of wheat — that’s a normal year, not great, not terrible. For maize, about 800 jin per mu. I don’t try to get the highest yield. I just need enough for us to eat and a little extra to sell. Spending too much to chase a big crop is gambling, and at my age I can’t afford to lose.

All together, this year will cost me about 2,600 yuan. That’s most of our cash savings. It frightens me to spend it all, but if I don’t, we’ll have nothing to harvest.
